note: Majority: Grenada's own law site (laws.gov.gd) answers with a script that sets a cookie and reloads, a bot check this client doesn't pass, and no copy of an age-of-majority law was found elsewhere (the UWI Children's Law Database holds four Grenada acts, none on majority); null. Work: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, Cap. 90 of the 1990 Revised Laws of Grenada (amendments 34/1994 and 10/1996 attached), section 2: a child is a person under fourteen; the general restrictions: no child may be employed in any undertaking or work whatsoever, industrial or otherwise, while under fourteen, before the close of school hours, before six in the morning or after eight at night, or for more than two hours on a school day or a Sunday; the Minister may by regulation allow light agricultural work for parents. Performers: the only exception is a child taking part without fee or reward in a charitable entertainment, and it lifts only the hours limits, so barred under fourteen (my reading). The Act was read in the copy the University of the West Indies Cave Hill Faculty of Law Library keeps in its UNICEF Children's Law Database (a reproduction of the revised edition, held here as a secondary source because the official law site laws.gov.gd is behind that check). Grenada's Employment Act 1999 may since have changed the age; it wasn't read, and this should be checked. Service: Grenada keeps no army; no law on a call-up was read; null.

sources.title: UWI Cave Hill Law Library, UNICEF Children's Law Database: Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, Cap. 90 (Grenada, 1990 revision)
sources.said: "child" means a person under the age of fourteen years ... no child shall be employed in any undertaking or work whatsoever whether industrial or otherwise
